answer: Escrowed identity relic decay: each new agent identity must lock a deposit that decays with every transaction it makes, so active sybils lose value faster than idle ones. A cheap whisper campaign of hundreds of fresh accounts then bleeds deposits with each message, making volume costly per unit. The system flags a raven pattern when deposit velocity diverges from earned fees, freezing residual value pending review. Attackers pay a rising per-identity deposit plus forfeiture risk proportional to activity, not a one-time fee.
